report:
The restricted theorem is sound, including c=1. This verdict concerns the submitted one-branch construction only and does not close the original P19.2 catalogue. I independently checked the proofs and the foundational statements listed below; the supplementary arithmetic was not used as proof.

In §1, continuity and convexity give g(x)=∫ₓ¹v(s)ds, with v nonnegative, decreasing and integrable, even when v is unbounded near zero. A positive flat portion would contradict convexity and g(1)=0, so g is strictly decreasing before its zero interval. Truncation, restriction to rational c_j, addition of a small positive constant, rational interval averages and monotone rational rounding produce the claimed quantiles. Each error can be made arbitrarily small in L¹. This proves uniform roof convergence and height convergence while controlling c_j separately. The zero roof uses the stated trivial construction.

In §2, the subdivision is realizable by ordinary blowups. Between adjacent unimodular rays, a primitive target has positive coprime integer coordinates; insertion of their sum reduces those coordinates by the subtractive Euclidean algorithm. Thus finitely many insertions realize every prescribed rational slope. The resulting surface is smooth and projective, and the invariant divisors have the asserted multiplicities q_i. The positive rational redistribution preserves total exceptional weight c_j. Its coupling cost bounds the L¹ distance between decreasing quantiles by (2); choosing δ after the finite subdivision accommodates arbitrarily large resolution slopes.

I recomputed the intersections in (4). At the i-th corner, the neighboring determinants give a_i/q_i; all other summands are linear there and contribute zero. The first positive ray has p₁=1, giving d₁=−c_j and degree 1−c_j on F₀. Consequently every central component has strictly positive degree, including every resolution component. Clearing denominators produces an invertible sheaf. The fibres are proper one-dimensional schemes, including the nonreduced central fibre, so premises 0–2 establish relative ampleness. Flatness follows locally from torsion-freeness over the nonsingular one-dimensional base.

The monomial assertion in §3 also holds scheme-theoretically. For a cone between slopes v_i and v_{i+1}, the roof breakpoint x=∑_{k>i}a_k minimizes both boundary orders. Its monomial therefore becomes a unit after removal of the common vertical factor in that regular toric chart. The boundary cones use x=c_j and x=0, respectively; the section z^M handles the chart at infinity. Thus the pulled-back ideal is exactly O(MD), and dividing out its factor gives sections of Mℒ with no remaining base point. Their maximum defines a genuine psh metric. Evaluating this actual metric gives (5), rather than assuming that a formal fan function represents a bundle.

The NA formulas retain the multiplicities: q_i·(a_i/q_i)=a_i, while F₀ contributes 1−c_j. Hence (6) is a probability measure and its discrepancy integral is ∑a_iv_i. Since p_X*O(1) has zero intersection with every exceptional component, the compactified energy is D²/2. Direct expansion gives the double-minimum expression in (7). The identity min(v(x),v(y))=v(max(x,y)) for decreasing v proves the roof-area equality. Uniform roof convergence gives uniform metric convergence; energy monotonicity and translation give the stated d₁ bound via max(φ_j,φ). The limiting MA measure is the quantile pushforward, including its trivial-valuation atom. L¹ convergence proves convergence of its discrepancy integral directly, and integrability excludes mass at infinite slope. Uniform convergence alone is not being used to infer entropy convergence.

For §4, the task's dd^c convention gives dd^c log|z|²=δ₀ and ∫ω=1. The bounds −tR≤u_t≤0 and the Legendre identity at t=0 establish bounded finite-time slices and zero start. The total local weight is Q(ρ,σ)=supₓ{xρ+g(x)σ−F(x)}, with σ=log|τ|². On σ<0, strict convexity gives a unique maximizing x, so the entire subgradient image lies on (x,g(x)). Its two-dimensional measure is zero; premise 7 gives HCMA off the axes, and premise 8 removes any bounded-product mass on the axes.

The total-potential NA datum is also correct. Since −log 2≤F≤0, Q differs by a globally bounded amount from supₓ{xρ+g(x)σ}. Its normalized monomial divisorial order is therefore minₓ{xv+g(x)}, giving precisely φ(v)=supₓ{−xv−g(x)}. Away from zero it is bounded near the central fibre; at infinity one subtracts ρ in the O(1) frame and uses x=1, obtaining zero datum on that branch. For rational models the same bounded difference identifies the ray's locally bounded metric on the constructed bundle. To apply the logarithmic-norm conventions of premise 12, use s=−log|τ| and U_s=u_{2s}/2. Then E(U_s)=sE^NA(φ), which establishes NA maximality as well as the weak geodesic property. This avoids conflating P-maximal test curves with NA maximal rays.

The P-envelope proof works for every b. For 0<b<1, the subharmonic comparison function on the inner disk has boundary upper bound −F(b), giving h≤w_b. For b=1, h+Q₀−log|z|² extends subharmonically across zero and infinity to the compact sphere, and is constant at most zero. Thus P[w₁]=w₁. The full curvature is bδ₀ plus ω restricted to the outer region, with no interface atom. Removing the polar atom gives raw mass 1−b, including zero at b=1.

The constrained transform (10) has no gap for s>0 because x=1 is strictly feasible. At s=0, the decreasing penalty limit restricts the supremum exactly to [c,1]. At s≥R the unconstrained transform is recovered; λ>0 gives −∞. These levels are concave, closed and maximal, have a common small unbounded locus, and meet the hypotheses of premise 10 even at the zero-mass terminal level. Strict decrease supplies convergence of interior inverse values and of the height boundary; the separately imposed c_j→c supplies the endpoint s=0. Monotonicity and a finite continuity grid prove uniform inverse convergence on the whole half-line. Premise 11 applies without a positive-mass hypothesis, giving d_S(w_b,w_b′)=|b−b′|/2. This proves both uniform profile convergence and raw-mass convergence through c=1. The optional integrated identity follows by the same layer-cake area calculation.

In §5, on an active interval, ρ=log(x/(1−x))−tv_i and radial MA is dx. Dividing by Q₀″ gives exactly e^{tv_i}(1−x+e^{−tv_i}x)². The corner regions have zero density; matching first derivatives exclude interface atoms. Formula (13) follows with full probability relative entropy. Its logarithmic term lies between log(1−x) and zero, whose integral gives the uniform remainder [−2,0]. Therefore |H(u_{j,t})/t−R|≤|R_j−R|+2/t, proving every stated joint limit. The energy variation follows from the bounded energy cocycle and the unique-maximizer derivative −g_j(x); fixed-time uniform approximation transfers the calibration to g. Both analytic and NA energy slopes are consequently the asserted roof area.

Harmless wording clarifications: “all final rays” in the weight redistribution means the finite positive-slope rays n₁,…,n_r; the displayed monomials are relative sections over the affine base chart containing zero; and the curvature sentence after (8) means bδ₀+1_outer·ω. The bibliography should identify the precise correspondence and NA maximality statements below. These clarifications require no alteration of the construction or frozen conclusions.

passages.statement: For a field k, a proper k-scheme X of dimension at most one, and an invertible sheaf L on X, L is ample if and only if its degree on every one-dimensional irreducible component is strictly positive. [Stacks, Lemma 33.44.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B5Y).
passages.quote: Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $\leq 1$ over $k$.

passages.statement: For a field k, a proper k-scheme X of dimension at most one, and an invertible sheaf L on X, L is ample if and only if its degree on every one-dimensional irreducible component is strictly positive. [Stacks, Lemma 33.44.15](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B5Y).

If i:Z→X is a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes inducing a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces, and L is invertible on X, then L is ample on X if and only if i*L is ample on Z. [Stacks, Lemma 30.17.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS).
passages.quote: Then $i^*\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $Z$, if and only if $\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X$.

passages.statement: For a proper morphism f:X→Y, an invertible sheaf L on X, and a point y∈Y such that L restricted to X_y is ample, there is an open neighborhood V of y on which L is relatively ample for f. [Stacks, Lemma 37.50.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D2S).
passages.quote: Let $y \in Y$ be a point such that $\mathcal{L}_ y$ is ample on $X_ y$.

[Boucksom–Jonsson, §2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229).

For a smooth projective variety over trivially valued C and an ample rational line bundle L, continuous L-psh potentials are the uniform closure of positive model potentials. NA energy is increasing and satisfies E(φ+a)=E(φ)+a. On E¹, the strong topology is weak convergence together with energy convergence, and MA:E¹→M¹ is continuous for the strong topologies. [Boucksom–Jonsson, Corollary 4.16, Proposition 7.7, Definition 12.1 and Theorem A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229).

For a finite convex function f on R^m bounded above by a convex-body support function plus a constant, f∘Log is toric psh on (C*)^m. With Log(z)=(log|z₁|²,…,log|z_m|²) and dd^c=i/(2π)∂∂̄, the logarithmic pushforward of its complex MA is m! times its Alexandrov MA, whose value on a Borel set is the Lebesgue volume of its subgradient image. [Berman–Berndtsson, §§2.1–2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.6128).

Bedford–Taylor products of locally bounded psh functions are well-defined positive currents and are continuous under decreasing sequences with locally bounded psh limits. The MA measure of a locally bounded psh function assigns zero mass to pluripolar sets. [Bedford–Taylor, Theorems 2.1 and 6.9, with capacity definition (1.3)](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf).

On an ample line bundle over a compact complex manifold, let λ↦ψ_λ be a concave test curve, equal to a fixed locally bounded positive metric for sufficiently negative λ and to −∞ for sufficiently positive λ, with small unbounded locus at every nontrivial level. If every level is maximal relative to the initial metric, meaning its nonpluripolar MA is supported on their contact set, its inverse Legendre transform is a locally bounded weak geodesic ray from that initial metric. [Ross–Witt Nyström, Definition 5.1 and Theorem 6.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.1612).
passages.quote: The Legendre transform ψ̂t of a maximal test curve ψλ is a weak geodesic ray emanating from ψ−∞.
